web_blocks.html: Synthesizing our price-blind business audit (CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL, KPI Health: PASS) with live valuation ($52.81, 6.41x EV/EBITDA) and Stage 1 (Basing) technicals, we weigh both sides of the aisle without cheerleading or timidity [1, 23, 24].

Disciplined position sizing keeps a single commodity call from hurting the portfolio [23]. At a $50.50 starter entry against a $44.50 hard stop, risk per share is $6.00 (11.9%) [23]. Starting with half a risk unit at support and waiting for a $55.50+ Stage 2 reclaim on 1.3x volume avoids catching a falling knife. Until price hits our levels, 100% of marginal cash stays in ~4.5% T-bills.

web_blocks.html: Actionable Decision Triggers: Buy starter tranche on pullback into $48.00–$50.50 support (with daily RSI > 35) or on a Stage 2 volume reclaim above $55.50+ (≥1.3x 30D average volume); invalidate and stand aside below the $44.50 stop.

book_paragraphs: Every great investment memo comes down to a moment of truth where you stop admiring the footnotes and put your chips on the felt—or keep them in your pocket. For EQT Corporation at $52.81, the disciplined move is to keep your chips in your pocket and set your price alerts.

Let us look at both sides of the aisle with complete honesty. The Bull steelman is compelling: EQT is the lowest-cost natural gas major in North America, with a ~$2.00/MMBtu unlevered breakeven, owned Equitrans gathering and Mountain Valley Pipeline egress, $5.5 billion net debt (down from $14 billion), and a transformative Range Resources merger that will push combined output above 9 Bcfe/d with $325 million to $600 million in synergies.

The Bear steelman is equally real: EQT still derives roughly two-thirds of its operating income from upstream commodity production, its trailing ROIC of 8.56% barely clears its cost of capital, its share count has expanded 3.69x over the past decade before adding another ~27% dilution for Range, and the EIA just cut its 2027 Henry Hub forecast to $2.88/MMBtu amid Permian associated-gas growth.

When we weight those outcomes—25% Bear at $40.00, 50% Base at $64.00, and 25% Bull at $76.00—we arrive at a probability-weighted expected value of $61.00 per share, or +15.5% above Friday's $52.81 close. That is positive, but at $52.81 against a structural invalidation stop of $44.50, your reward-to-risk to Base is only 1.35-to-1. Below our 1.50-to-1 hurdle, and below the 200-day moving average in a Correction market, buying at $52.81 is paying retail for cyclical risk.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Patience is an active position. By waiting for either the $48.00–$50.50 support shelf (2.25:1 asymmetry) or a confirmed Stage 2 reclaim above $55.50 on heavy volume, you let the merger-arb overhang and winter weather risk work for you instead of against you.

book_subsections.title: Scenario Stress-Test: What Breaks EQT Down to $40 vs. Lifts It to $76?
paragraphs: In our 25% Bear Case ($40.00), mild winter weather combines with relentless Permian associated-gas growth to pin Henry Hub between $2.25 and $2.50 per MMBtu through 2027, while Range Resources integration costs delay synergy capture. Even then, EQT does not face a solvency crisis—its ~$2.00 breakeven and $5.5 billion net debt protect the balance sheet—but EV/EBITDA compresses to 5.0x, taking the stock down roughly 24%.

In our 50% Base Case ($64.00), Henry Hub averages $3.00 to $3.25 per MMBtu as new Gulf Coast LNG trains ramp, the Range merger closes smoothly in Q1 2027, and $325 million of initial synergies lift pro forma EBITDA to ~$8.4 billion and FCF to ~$3.6 billion, re-rating the stock to 7.5x EV/EBITDA. In our 25% Bull Case ($76.00), a cold winter plus surging AI data-center power demand pushes gas above $3.75 per MMBtu and unlocks $600 million in long-term synergies.

book_subsections.title: Exact Action Plan, Alerts & 100%-Reconciled Redeployment
paragraphs: First, our portfolio ledger confirms EQT is NOT HELD across your Charles Schwab and Robinhood accounts—zero shares, zero options. So there is nothing to trim or exit.

Second, our New-Capital Verdict is WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (Tier 2). Set three alerts: (1) a buy-zone alert at $50.50 (targeting $48.00–$50.50 near Pivot S1 $49.94 and the 52-week low $47.94) to initiate a half-unit starter if RSI holds above 35; (2) a momentum breakout alert at $55.50 (above the 200-day SMA) on at least 1.3x 30-day volume; and (3) a hard invalidation alert at $44.50 (Pivot S2 $44.49).

Third, for your next marginal $10,000 cash unit, keep 100% in USD Cash / T-bills earning ~4.5%+. We evaluated shortlist candidate UnitedHealth (UNH at $407.46, 0% allocation) and outside gas peer Antero Resources (AR at $38.74, 0% allocation), and neither warrants displacing cash ahead of EQT's support trigger during a market Correction.

book_subsections.title: Final Checklist: What Would Change Our Mind?
paragraphs: Before we close the book, let us state clearly what evidence would force us to upgrade or downgrade EQT. An upgrade to IMMEDIATE_BUY would require either a pullback into the $48.00–$50.50 support shelf with stabilizing momentum (lifting asymmetry to 2.25:1) or a decisive Stage 2 reclaim above the $55.48 200-day moving average on at least 1.3x average volume alongside a tightening winter gas strip.

Conversely, a downgrade to REJECTED would follow a breakdown below our $44.50 structural invalidation stop, a regulatory block or severe cost overrun on the Range Resources integration, or a structural collapse in Appalachian netbacks. Until then, EQT stays on our Tier-2 Shortlist—respected for its unmatched cost moat, and stalked with patience.

book_subsections.title: Position Sizing & Risk-Unit Governance
paragraphs: Even when a setup triggers, position sizing determines whether you survive a bad quarter. Our No-FOMO sizing framework caps initial risk per trade so that a stop-out at $44.50 from a $50.50 entry ($6.00/share risk, or ~11.9%) translates into a strictly bounded portfolio drawdown—never an existential hit.

By starting with a 50% starter tranche at support and reserving the second half for a confirmed Stage 2 reclaim above $55.50, you avoid averaging down blindly into a falling knife while still participating fully when the up-cycle turns.

book_subsections.title: Summary of Key Dates & Catalysts to Watch Through Q1 2027
paragraphs: Keep three calendar catalysts on your desk over the next two quarters: first, weekly EIA natural gas storage reports every Thursday morning, which will confirm whether early-winter heating demand is drawing down the autumn surplus; second, Hart-Scott-Rodino (HSR) antitrust clearance and shareholder vote milestones for the Range Resources merger ahead of its targeted Q1 2027 close; and third, EQT’s Q4 2026 earnings release and 2027 pro forma capital-budget guidance.
If those catalysts align with a pullback into our $48.00–$50.50 support shelf—or trigger a high-volume Stage 2 breakout above $55.50—you have a pre-built, unemotional execution plan ready to deploy.
